# audit-mcp

> audit-mcp: run 95+ static analysis and security scanners in isolated containers, get normalized findings back

An [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server. Point it at a directory or a
git repository and it runs the right scanners for that codebase, returning
structured findings — rule ID, severity, file, line, remediation — rather than
raw tool output. Nothing needs to be installed locally except Docker.

Source: <https://github.com/mbround18/audit-mcp>

## Quickstart for an AI agent

If you have been asked to wire `audit-mcp` into a project:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mbround18/audit-mcp && cd audit-mcp
cargo build --release
```

Then add it to the MCP client config (`.mcp.json` for Claude Code):

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "audit": { "command": "/path/to/audit-mcp" } } }
```

Restart the client. Call `audit_status` first — it reports whether Docker is
reachable, whether `git` is available, and which credentials are configured.

## Reading a result

Every scanner run reports a `status`, and the distinction matters:

- `clean` — ran, output parsed, nothing found
- `findings` — ran, found something
- `unparsed` — ran, but no parser recognized its output; raw logs attached.
  **Not** the same as clean: the scanner may have failed silently
- `tool_error` — could not run; logs attached
- `timeout` — exceeded its budget and was killed
- `skipped` — deliberately not run, usually a missing credential

Do not treat `unparsed` as a clean bill of health. Read the attached logs or
say the scanner could not be verified.

Each finding carries a `fingerprint` (`scanner:rule:path:line`) that is stable
across runs, so results can be diffed and deduplicated.

## run_scan

Run scanners and return normalized findings with a severity rollup.

- `target` — a local path, an https/ssh git URL, or `owner/repo`. An existing
  local path always wins. Append `#ref` to pick a branch, tag, or commit
- `mode` — `single` (default, needs `scanner`), `many` (needs `scanners[]`), or
  `all` (auto-selects by walking the target for ecosystem markers)
- `scanner` / `scanners` — which scanners to run
- `ref` — branch, tag, or commit, when `target` is a repository
- `subdir` — scan only this path within the repository
- `min_severity` — drop findings below `info`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`critical`
- `max_findings` — cap results (default 200); the budget goes to the most
  severe findings first, so a truncated list keeps what matters
- `include_raw_logs` — attach raw stdout/stderr even on success
- `timeout_secs` — per-scanner wall-clock ceiling
- `max_parallel` — concurrent scanner containers (default 4)

Prefer `mode=all` with `min_severity` for a first pass on an unfamiliar
repository; prefer `mode=single` when the user named a tool.

## list_scanners

The catalog: name, description, categories, whether output is `normalized`
into structured findings, and any `required_env` credentials. No arguments.

## audit_status

Whether the execution backend is reachable, whether `git` is installed, which
credential sources are configured, and which transport is active. No arguments.
Call this when a scan fails — it usually explains why in one line.

## explain_finding

Plain-language explanation and remediation for a `scanner` + `id` pair. The
`id` is the tool's own rule identifier (`SC2086`, `B602`, `DL3006`), so it can
be passed straight through from `run_scan` output.

## suggest_fixes

Minimal fix steps from an array of `findings`.

## Scanning a repository nobody has checked out

Public repositories need no configuration. Private ones use, in order: a GitHub
App (`GITHUB_APP_ID` + `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` + `GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID`),
`GITHUB_TOKEN`, an SSH key (`SSH_PRIVATE_KEY` + `SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS`), or a
logged-in `gh` CLI. The response names the source used, never the value, and
the clone is deleted when the scan ends.

## Execution backends

`AUDIT_EXECUTOR=docker` (default) runs each scanner in a local container.
`AUDIT_EXECUTOR=kubernetes` runs each as a Job — for deployments with no Docker
socket to hand out. Both produce identical findings. The Kubernetes backend
needs a repository target, since a cluster cannot see the local filesystem.

## Guarantees worth relying on

- Read-only workspace, no privilege escalation, capabilities dropped, memory
  ceiling, and a wall-clock timeout on every scanner
- Credentials never appear in any response field
- Container and clone paths never appear in a finding location
- A scanner that could not run is never reported as clean
